summary: All 20 supplied occurrences checked. The reader overcounts the current Infectum examples and calls 71/42 already filed; the supplied entry contains two, neither 71/42. Its absolute resistance context is therefore added.
Detransitive 1 is a lexical happening/befalling function, not merely a Detransitive counterpart of resisting. ʕal codes the affected person; bala, taǧraba or ʕiš can be the event subject.
PrS 82/23-24 heaping was checked against full kwm II and the matching mqawamlan quotation under gnw. It is not secure evidence of qwm polysemy; no material is written to the other roots' entries.
mqam at Talay 1/305 is a contracted event predicate with the same question function, not a new stem.

The inherited Detransitive Preterit-wa example 110/28 has mqaqam-wa and no translation. Allowed text 110/21 has mqawəm without -wa and a matching calamity clause; 110/28 was not found in the supplied R110 text. Do not manufacture a Preterit-wa translation from a different form.
The active opposition sense remains distinct from the inherited Detransitive happening/befalling sense. No Jan occurrence securely adds to the latter.
Maqəmiwo is formally close to qym III and is only tentatively linked to qwm through the resistance interpretation. It is withheld from a new II Infectum-wa box until the root/formation is settled.

The drinking-warning example has mqawamlox in a relative sequence with a human counterpart and d oṯe mqabəl diḏox. It supports confrontation under existing II.1 provisionally; a new direct-object government rule is not inferred.
The oldest active Infectum cell is full after round 1. Routine resistance at Jan 2.3/338 is not added from the reader's stale thin-cell count.
Are mqawamme/mqawamlan in PrS 82/23-24 q variants of kwm II, source spelling errors or a distinct qwm lexeme? Confirm before transferring the examples or numbering a new qwm sense.
Verify the inherited 110/28 mqaqam-wa citation and form against the edition. Should it instead be the Preterit mqawəm at 110/21, and should the unsupported Preterit-wa box be removed?
What implicit feminine circumstance or need licenses miqawmo in 106/26?
Does the offensive confrontation in PrS 2/17 warrant a narrower subsense, or does existing es aufnehmen cover it as proposed?
At Jan 2.7/1826 is maqəmiwo contracted qwm II or qym III? The ʕal complement and resistance context alone cannot settle the stem.

At Jan 2.10/2307 segment mqawamlox and identify its subject: is -lox a second-person agent or an affected/addressee suffix? Does the relative head fill an omitted opponent position? The example is provisional.
Does mqawəm with a writer indicate a lexical endurance sense or pragmatic resistance to difficulties? Current evidence is treated as an extension of II.1.
Provide verified translations for Jan; machine-English participant assignments are not copied into published examples.
Opposition covers armed confrontation and domestic demands, not only defensive resistance; ʕal remains the opponent frame.

A writer's mqawəm w mkaməl over a lifetime gives a perseverance application of resistance. Round 1 already supplies absolute mqawmina without an expressed opponent; absence of ʕal alone does not establish a new sense.
